identification.summary: APT.3102 is a name for the actor behind a variant of the '9002' Trojan called '3102', which Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 reported in September 2015 after two spear-phishing attacks that used the same lure document [S1]. The name comes from the string '3102', which the payload uses as the first four bytes of its network communications [S1]. Malpedia lists the group as APT.3102 and cites the Unit 42 report as its reference [S3].
identification.firstObserved: Unit 42 observed the two spear-phishing attacks on 2015-05-06 and 2015-05-11 [S1]. Unit 42 also cites a Cylance article on a May 2014 targeted attack against a Chinese national that delivered the 3102 variant of 9002 [S1].
identification.notes: Unit 42 says the 3102 payload appears related to the Evilgrab payload used in a May 2015 watering-hole attack on the Myanmar president's website [S1][S2]. That is a payload relationship reported by one vendor, not a confirmed merge of actor clusters. No Microsoft name or MITRE group ID was found for this actor.

attribution.confidence: Unit 42 assessed that the C2 infrastructure ties to individuals in China who are active on hacking forums and claim to develop Trojans [S1]. No source reviewed attributes the activity to a specific government organization.
attribution.basis: Unit 42 infrastructure analysis linking C2 to individuals in China, and the payload similarity to Evilgrab [S1][S2]. The encyclopedia country field (CN) is carried from the imported record.

targeting.notes: Unit 42 observed one spear-phishing attack on a US government target and one on a European media company, using the same lure document [S1]. The related Evilgrab watering hole targeted the Myanmar president's website [S2].

capabilities.summary: Spear-phishing with a weaponized delivery document that installs the 3102 variant of the 9002 Trojan, which relies heavily on plugins [S1]. The payload uses the string '3102' as the first four bytes of its C2 communications [S1]. A related Evilgrab payload was delivered in the May 2015 Myanmar watering hole, in which an IFRAME was injected into a Drupal theme JavaScript file [S2].

campaigns.name: Targeted attack on a Chinese national (Cylance)
campaigns.summary: Unit 42 cites a Cylance article on a targeted attack against a Chinese national that delivered the 3102 variant of 9002 [S1].

campaigns.name: Spear-phishing of a US government target
campaigns.summary: Unit 42 observed a spear-phishing attack on a US government target using a weaponized document that installed the 3102 payload [S1].

campaigns.name: Spear-phishing of a European media company
campaigns.summary: Unit 42 observed a second attack, using the same lure document, against a European media company [S1].

campaigns.name: Evilgrab watering hole on the Myanmar president's website (related payload)
campaigns.summary: Unit 42 reported a watering hole that delivered an Evilgrab variant. Unit 42 said it had evidence of access to the site since November 2014 or earlier. The 3102 payload appears related to Evilgrab [S1][S2].

diamond.adversary: Unit 42 tied the C2 infrastructure to individuals in China active on hacking forums [S1].
diamond.capability: Spear-phishing documents; the 3102 variant of 9002, which is plugin-based; a related Evilgrab payload [S1][S2].
diamond.infrastructure: C2 infrastructure that Unit 42 linked to individuals in China [S1]. Further details were not accessible.
diamond.victim: A US government target and a European media company [S1].

gaps: I could not open the primary Unit 42 reports. WebFetch failed with a DNS error, so the content above comes from WebSearch result summaries only. Re-verify against the Unit 42 articles before use [S1][S2].
The exploit and CVE used in the lure document, the C2 domains and the indicators were not obtained.
No sponsor, no government attribution and no stated objective were found. The 'individuals in China' language does not establish state sponsorship.
Whether APT.3102 is the same cluster as the Evilgrab actor, or maps to groups in other vendors' naming, is unresolved.
No activity after 2015 was found in the results. The Cylance 2014 article was not reviewed.
Malpedia lists no malware families for this actor [S3]. The Malpedia page itself could not be fetched.
